surface_mechanism_description: The generation of –OH groups on the surface during the water pulse due to its dissociative adsorption on oxide surfaces explains the enhanced growth rate with water as the oxygen source. The growth rate increase at lower temperatures is related to the increased content of –OH groups on the surface when using water as the oxygen source.
evidence: When using water as the oxygen source the growth experiments were conducted at temperature range of 75–250 uC (Fig. 2b). A region of constant growth rate ( y0.8 Å/cycle) could be observed between 125 and 200 uC and self-limited growth was confirmed at 150 uC. It should be noted that with water the growth rate is considerably higher than when using ozone as the oxygen source. This enhanced growth rate might be explained by the generation of the –OH groups on the surface during the water pulse due to its dissociative adsorption on oxide surfaces. 31 An increase of the growth rate at the lower temperature is already observable at 100 uC with the water process. While the physisorption of the precursor might already play a role in the growth at 100 uC, this increase in growth rate can also be related to the increased content of –OH groups on the surface at lower temperatures, especially when using water as the oxygen source.
